To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a neural correlate of spatial attention, the N2p, is modulated by attentional filtering.
attentional filtering has an electrophysiological correlate, the N2pC, that is observed only when filtering is necessary and is not observed in the absence of filtering.
attentional filtering during visual search has a neural correlate and that the neural correlate of attentional filtering occurs after a preliminary feature analysis of the stimulus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural correlates of visual attention.
the neural mechanisms underlying the selection of relevant information in complex visual scenes.
the neural mechanisms of attentional selection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N2pc reflects attentional filtering in occipital areas after a preliminary feature analysis.

the N2pc is a neural correlate of the attentional selection of a single object within an array, and that this selection occurs after a preliminary analysis of the array as a whole, but before a detailed analysis of the selected object.
the N2pc component of the event-related potential waveform reflects the deployment of attentional filtering during visual search.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N2pc component of the ERP is a neural marker of spatial filtering during visual search.
the N2pc is a marker of attentional filtering that is under the control of higher level processes and that it occurs in occipito-temporal cortex.

attentional filtering is a top-down process that is initiated by the selection of a target template and that is implemented in visual areas by means of a spatially selective suppression of distractor items.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N2pc is a reliable marker for attentional filtering in the visual system.
the brain is capable of filtering out competing distractors during visual search.
attentional filtering has a neural correlate in the form of the N2pc component of the event-related potential waveform.
